paragraphs.source_en: MEHMED IV: BOY SULTAN TO MANLY SULTAN In summer 1648, Janissaries, jurists (including Sheikhulislam Karac¢elebizade), and a big crowd referred to by some Ottoman chroniclers as ‘the public’ (representing the will of the people) marched to the third gate, the Gate of Felicity, of Topkap1 Palace, site of enthronements. They demanded the dethronement of Ibrahim I and the enthronement of his oldest son, Prince Mehmed, in his place. At the anteroom to the third gate, Kosem Sultan—the spouse of (deceased) Ahmed I, the mother of (deceased) Murad IV and of Ibrahim I, and the grandmother of Prince Mehmed— upbraided the rebels for agreeing to whatever Ibrahim I had de-sired, stating, ‘Now you want to replace him with a-small child. What an evil plan this is. This crime of sedition is your doing’."* She demanded to know how a seven-year-old could be king.
